Metadata.title: InnerOS — Institut Mindset en Action®
Metadata.description: Collective and anonymous assessment of psychosocial risks at work.

Home.title: InnerOS
Home.tagline: Collective measurement of well-being at work, in support of the MINDSET® method.
Home.intro: InnerOS enables the Institut Mindset en Action® to run anonymous questionnaire campaigns in a client company, calculate collective scores and prepare a report validated by an IMA practitioner.
Home.principleAnonymity: Full anonymity: no account, no name, no address for respondents.
Home.principleThreshold: No result is shown for a group of fewer than 10 people.
Home.principleHuman: AI prepares a draft; an IMA practitioner checks and validates every report.
Home.principleNoDiagnosis: A collective prevention approach, never an individual diagnosis.

QuestionsTypes.help: Template questions validated by IMA for this mandate type. The chosen text replaces the content of the field below and remains editable: complete the parts in square brackets.
QuestionsTypes.confirmReplace: Replace the current text of the diagnostic question?
flash: What is the overall state of the psychosocial factors perceived by staff, and which points deserve priority attention?
Which aspects of work are perceived as resources, and which as points of concern?
Do the collective results point to areas that should be explored through a more comprehensive diagnosis?
n1: How do staff perceive their working conditions across the six MINDSET® levels: work, roles, interactions, management, organisation, environment?
Which psychosocial factors are perceived as the most favourable and the most concerning, and how do they vary from one group to another?
What collective prevention priorities emerge from the results?
n2: How do teams perceive their workload, their autonomy and the support they have received since [the change / the reorganisation of …]?
What differences in perception appear between [units / sites / roles] regarding job demands and available resources?
Which factors related to roles and working relationships (role clarity, support from colleagues, recognition, quality of line management) stand out as points of concern?
n3: How have the perceived psychosocial factors changed since the previous measurement in [month / year]?
How have perceptions changed in the areas targeted by the [year] action plan?
What priorities emerge for the next phase of the prevention plan?

Kit.title: Information note for workers and their representatives
Kit.subtitle: Anonymous questionnaire on well-being at work — {entreprise}
Kit.workingVersion: Working version — text to be validated by the Institut Mindset en Action® before distribution
Kit.why: {entreprise} has asked the Institut Mindset en Action® (IMA) to carry out a collective assessment of psychosocial factors at work: workload, autonomy, relationships, support, organisation and well-being. The aim is to identify, together, ways of improving collective prevention. It is in no way an assessment of individuals.
Kit.how: Each person receives a card with a single-use code and a QR code. The questionnaire takes about 20 minutes, on a phone or a computer. First you select your group ({critere}) from a list, then you answer the questions.
Kit.anonymity1: No account, no name, no email address and no IP address is recorded.
Kit.anonymity2: The code is not linked to any name: no list connects a code to a person.
Kit.anonymity3: Only the date is kept, never the time.
Kit.anonymity4: Codes are deleted at the end of data collection.
Kit.anonymity5: No result is calculated for a group of fewer than {seuil} people.
Kit.anonymity6: No one, neither your employer nor IMA, can see an individual's answers.
Kit.who: IMA practitioners analyse collective results only. Your employer receives a collective report, validated by IMA, which may be presented to the workers' representatives. No individual answer is passed on to anyone.
Kit.free: You may decline to take part, skip a question (“I prefer not to answer”) or stop at any time, without any consequence. This questionnaire is not a medical examination and does not lead to any individual diagnosis.
Kit.ai: A first draft of the report is written with the help of an artificial intelligence (Claude, by the company Anthropic), based solely on the collective results. The AI does not see any individual answer, does not calculate the scores and makes no decision: an IMA practitioner checks, corrects and validates every report.
Kit.aiEu: This information is provided in accordance with the European regulation on artificial intelligence (Article 50).
Kit.toValidate: Text to be validated by a legal expert.
Kit.help: If you are going through a difficult time, you are not alone. Talk to someone you trust, to your doctor or to your company's prevention service. You can also contact:
Kit.contact: A question about this survey? Institut Mindset en Action® — info@institutmindsetenaction.com

BE.legal: In Belgium, employers are required to analyse psychosocial risks at work (Code on Well-being at Work, Book I, Title 3). This survey supports that analysis without replacing the role of the prevention adviser for psychosocial aspects, the confidential counsellor or the occupational physician. Before the survey, the employer informs and consults the workers' representatives (Committee for Prevention and Protection at Work or, failing that, the trade union delegation or the workers themselves).

aides.cps: Centre de Prévention du Suicide (suicide prevention, in French)

FR.legal: In France, employers assess occupational risks, including psychosocial risks, and record them in the single occupational risk assessment document (DUERP). The social and economic committee (CSE) is informed and consulted.

BR.legal: In Brazil, the NR-1 standard requires companies to identify and assess psychosocial risks as part of occupational risk management (GRO / PGR). This survey feeds into the GRO / PGR without replacing it, nor the role of the SESMT or the CIPA. NR-1 provides for worker participation.

aides.cvv: CVV — Centro de Valorização da Vida (suicide prevention)

PT.legal: In Portugal, employers assess occupational risks, including psychosocial risks, under the legal framework for the promotion of safety and health at work (Law No. 102/2009). Workers' representatives are informed and consulted.

Risques.title: Psychosocial risk register
Risques.intro: Each risk is assessed with the Kinney matrix: Risk = Probability × Exposure × Severity. The register is kept by IMA and by the organisation's prevention advisor.
Risques.deleteConfirm: Permanently delete this risk from the register?

gravites.1: Slight discomfort, no effect on health
gravites.3: Noticeable discomfort (occasional tension, loss of motivation)
gravites.7: Reversible harm without prolonged absence (marked fatigue, disturbed sleep, repeated tension)
gravites.15: Harm to health with absence of a few days to a few weeks
gravites.40: Lasting harm to physical or mental health, long-term absence
gravites.100: Danger to life or irreversible harm

Risques.noNames: Describe the situation without naming anyone: no names, email addresses or phone numbers.
Risques.groupsHelp: Only groups shown in the results (at least the campaign threshold).
Risques.proposalsHelp: InnerOS pre-fills each risk from the diagnosis: MINDSET® level, groups on the unfavourable side, probability (result read on the unfavourable side), daily exposure and severity (by type of risk, one step higher if the validated report cites it). These are suggestions (IMA convention, no national reference): change them if you disagree.
Risques.proposalsNone: No suggestions: a closed campaign is needed (and, for the prevention advisor, a report validated by IMA).
Risques.mandatory: Reported behaviour: must be recorded (class at least “high”)
Risques.manualHelp: For example after interviews, a field observation or an accident.
Risques.matrixClasses: Score above 400: very high · above 200: high · above 70: substantial · above 20: possible · 20 or less: acceptable. Reported offensive behaviour is always at least “high”.
Risques.advisorHelp: The appointed prevention advisor can keep the organisation's psychosocial risk register with IMA. They see a campaign's results only once the report has been validated.
Risques.importAll: Add all suggestions from campaign {reference} to the register
Risques.importHelp: The MINDSET® level, groups concerned and P, E and S values are pre-filled from the diagnosis and the validated report. Each risk can then be edited if you disagree with the suggested assessment.
Risques.imported: {n, plural, one {# risk added} other {# risks added}} to the register: check the suggested values.

Plan.title: Psychosocial risk prevention plan
Plan.intro: Five-year global prevention plan and first-year action plan, drawn up from the risk register and the validated report. Validated by an AI-trained IMA practitioner before the organisation can see them.
Plan.noReport: A validated report for one of this organisation's campaigns is needed first.
Plan.aiCost: Only the risk register (without names), the validated report, the sector, the size, the country and the internal code are sent. Estimated cost: about $0.15 to $0.25.
Plan.aiOff: AI is disabled (globally or for the report's campaign): manual writing only.
Plan.newVersion: New version based on the plan in force
Plan.questions: Questions for the practitioner (internal to IMA)
Plan.noName: A function, never a name (e.g. “Management”, “HR”, “team leaders”).
Plan.check_risques: Priority risks are covered and deadlines are realistic.
Plan.check_fonctions: Owners are designated by their function; no personal names.
Plan.check_cadre: The plan complies with the legal framework of the organisation's country.
Plan.check_langage: The IMA language rule is respected; no individual data.
Plan.validateHelp: Every “very high” or “high” risk and every reported offensive behaviour must have at least one action; a “very high” risk must have an action in Q1.
Plan.validated: Plan validated: it is now visible to the organisation's prevention advisor.
Plan.trainingMissing: Validation not possible: first record your AI training (IMA space home page).
Plan.mentionAi: Plan written with AI assistance and validated by {nom}, IMA practitioner.
Plan.mentionManual: Plan written and validated by {nom}, IMA practitioner.
Plan.spaceLink: Your organisation's psychosocial risk prevention plan
Plan.adoptionHelp: The plan validated by IMA is a proposal: the employer adopts it after consulting the body required by law. State the body consulted and the dates.
Plan.adoptionBE: Belgium: the annual action plan is submitted to the CPPT for advice before 1 November of the previous year.

organes.cppt: Committee for prevention and protection at work (CPPT)

Plan.avisLe: Date of the advice or consultation
Plan.avisLeHelp: Leave empty only if there is no CSE (France).
Plan.adoptedMeta: Adopted by {nom} on {date} · body consulted: {organe} (advice of {avis}).
Plan.notAdopted: Not yet adopted by the organisation.
Plan.progressReadOnly: Only the prevention advisor and IMA update progress.
Plan.commentHelp: No names, emails or phone numbers (500 characters max).
Plan.pdfFooter: Institut Mindset en Action® — psychosocial risk prevention plan, for the organisation and its representatives only
Plan.pdfDraft: PREVIEW — plan not validated, do not distribute
Plan.pluriprevHelp: The PluriPrev file contains the validated plan, the risk register and progress, without any names (the organisation's internal code only).
Plan.continueTitle: Continuation of the plan in force
Plan.nextYearHelp: Same five-year global plan. Actions not completed are carried over (with their progress); the year's action plan is then validated by IMA and adopted by the organisation.
Plan.nextYearAi: Draft the action plan with AI
Plan.lastYear: The global plan is in its 5th year: prepare a new global plan (a new diagnosis is recommended).

Sensibilisation.title: Theme library
Sensibilisation.intro: Psychosocial risk and mental health awareness themes offered to organisations: one kit per language (article, short message, poster, discussion questions, email to managers, « wellbeing quarter-hour » sheet). A theme is only offered once validated by an AI-trained IMA practitioner.
Sensibilisation.fieldCodeHelp: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (e.g. sleep-recovery).
Sensibilisation.fieldDayHelp: E.g. « 10 October — World Mental Health Day ».
Sensibilisation.fieldScalesHelp: Codes separated by commas (e.g. qd, wp): the theme will be suggested to organisations whose register reports these risks.
Sensibilisation.fieldSensitive: Sensitive theme (suicide, violence, harassment): stricter responsible communication rules
Sensibilisation.sensitiveWarning: Sensitive theme: review with particular care (no details about means, messages of hope, signposting to help). A review by a suicide prevention professional is recommended.
Sensibilisation.aiHelp: The AI only receives the theme sheet (title, objective, month, level, scales): no organisation data. Estimated cost: about $0.05. The current kit in this language is replaced.
Sensibilisation.supportAuto: The organisation's support people and the country's helplines are added automatically at the end of the kit: do not write them here.
Sensibilisation.kTips: Wellbeing quarter-hour: tips for the facilitator
Sensibilisation.saved: Saved. The theme stays a draft until it is validated.
Sensibilisation.generated: Kit drafted by AI: review it before validating the theme.
Sensibilisation.validateHelp: The French kit is required; every language started must be complete. Any later change returns the theme to draft.
Sensibilisation.validated: Theme validated: it can be offered to organisations.
Sensibilisation.trainingMissing: Validation not possible: first record your AI training (IMA space home page).
Sensibilisation.archiveHelp: An archived theme is no longer offered to organisations.
